gas-works.name: Gas Works Park
gas-works.blurb: The rusted towers of the last US coal-gasification plant on a lawn promontory in Lake Union, a kite hill with a mosaic sundial and a skyline view across the water.

spawn.note: Path between Kite Hill and the towers, skyline across the lake.

extent.description: Kite Hill with sundial, the fenced generator towers, Play Barn (painted exhauster-compressor building), Prow terrace on the south point, picnic shelter, lakeshore paths.
extent.edges: N Northlake Way + Burke-Gilman Trail (north); Lake Union shore (no water access — contaminated sediments; cleanup from 2027).
extent.vertical: Kite Hill summit ~20 m (OSM ele), park otherwise ~6–8 m above lake.

structures.name: Gas generator towers (1906–1956 plant)
structures.form: Cluster of tall riveted steel cylinders, pipes, ladders and catwalks, fenced off; rust-orange and black with streaks, graffiti traces; strongest silhouette in the park.
structures.safety_note: Do NOT make the towers climbable (fatal falls in 2012, 2022, 2025 per Wikipedia); fence + interpretive sign.

structures.name: Play Barn (former exhauster-compressor building)
structures.form: Open timber/steel shed with machinery painted in bright primary colours (red, yellow, blue, purple pipes and compressors) for kids to climb.

structures.name: Kite Hill + Gas Works Memorial Sundial (Charles Greening)
structures.form: Grassy artificial mound (built of rubble) ~20 m; at the top a circular sundial relief of concrete, brick, inlaid bronze and cast elements — you are the gnomon.

sources.url: https://www.openstreetmap.org (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) — extracts in game/research/osm/sea-spots/

signage.where: entrance sign by the parking area

vegetation: Wide lawns, few trees (5 mapped), berm with trees along the old railway on the north
furniture: 5 benches, picnic shelter, bike racks, drinking fountain (OSM)

lighting.day: Open, bright; towers backlit at sunset from the west
lighting.night: Little lighting; city skyline glow across the lake; July 4th fireworks over Lake Union

backdrop: Downtown skyline + Space Needle across Lake Union (≈3 km SSW)
Seaplanes (Kenmore Air) landing on the lake, sailboats, houseboats
Aurora Bridge and Queen Anne hill to the west
I-5 Ship Canal Bridge to the east

crowd.density: Medium; kite flyers, picnics, dog walkers, photographers; huge crowd for July 4th fireworks.

plaques.title: Last gasworks
plaques.text: Gas Works Park holds the remnants of the sole remaining coal-gasification plant in the United States (1906–1956).

plaques.title: Richard Haag
plaques.text: Landscape architect Richard Haag kept the plant as an industrial ruin; the park opened in 1975.

plaques.title: Strangest park
plaques.text: A Seattle Times-affiliated site called it "easily the strangest park in Seattle and may rank among the strangest in the world".

interaction.primary: Fly a kite on Kite Hill (wind from real weather; higher wind = higher kite).
secondary: Stand on the sundial at the right spot to read the time

alternates.name: Skyline from Kite Hill
alternates.frame: Lake Union with downtown and the Space Needle

dialogueGeneral.usage: Pedestrian set for the Seattle and Bellevue driving districts and as filler in every spot. ctx: greeting|bumped|photographed|idle|spot|rain|honked_at|near_miss; non-English lines carry orig+lang with English text.

tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.
